## Detecting Digital Payment Fraud

The title of my project is *Detecting Digital Payment Fraud*. This will be a classification problem. Classifying digital payments as either fraudulent or not.



### Research Goals
  - Compare how well different classification models can detect fraud.
  - Discover which variables are most significant for detecting fraud.
  - Interpret results from the different classification models.
  
  

### Data Source:
[Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jayjoshi37/digital-payment-fraud-detection?select=Digital_Payment_Fraud_Detection_Dataset.csv)



### Data Description

There are 7,500 rows. There are 15 columns. The dependent variable is `fraud_label` and this is the variable I will predict. There are some categorical variables like `transaction_type` and `payment_mode` that I can use in the model. There are also many quantitative variables, such as `account_age_days`, `ip_risk_score`, `previous_failed_attempts`, that can also be used to predict `fraud_label`.

```{r descrp, warning=FALSE,message=FALSE,echo=F}
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, janitor)

fraud_data <- read_csv("Digital_Payment_Fraud_Detection_Dataset.csv")
fraud_data <- clean_names(fraud_data)

fraud_data <- fraud_data |>
  mutate(
    fraud_label = as.factor(fraud_label),
    transaction_type = as.factor(transaction_type),
    payment_mode = as.factor(payment_mode),
    device_type = as.factor(device_type)
  )


glimpse(fraud_data)
```



### Discuss Variables



```{r dependent, echo=FALSE}
# barchart for each class
ggplot(fraud_data,
       aes(x=fraud_label,fill=fraud_label))+
  geom_bar(color="black")+
  labs(
    title="Count of Dependent Variable Classes",
    y = "Count",
    x= "Class"
  )+
  geom_text(stat = "count",
    aes(label = after_stat(count)),
    vjust = -0.5
  )+
  theme_minimal()

```

This barchart shows us that there are 7011 transactions that are not fraudulent and 489 transactions that are. (0=no fraud, 1=fraud) 





```{r boxplot,echo=FALSE}
ggplot(fraud_data,
       aes(y=transaction_amount,fill=fraud_label))+
  geom_boxplot(color="black")+
  labs(
    title="Distribution of Transaction Amounts by Legitimacy",
    x = "Fraud Label",
    y = "Amount (USD)"
  )+
  theme_minimal()
```

Boxplot of `transaction_amount` sorted by `fraud_label`. The distributions look nearly identical, however this variable could still be useful in the classification models. 

```{r payment,echo=FALSE}
ggplot(fraud_data,
       aes(x=payment_mode,fill=payment_mode))+
  geom_bar(color="black")+
  labs(
    title="Count of Payment Modes",
    y = "Count",
    x= "Payment Mode"
  )+
  geom_text(stat = "count",
    aes(label = after_stat(count)),
    vjust = -0.5
  )+
  theme_minimal()
```

Bar chart of `payment_mode`. This shows that there are 4 types of payments in this dataset and there is about an equal amount of each.




```{r barchartbypay, echo = F}
ggplot(fraud_data,
       aes(x=fraud_label,fill=payment_mode))+
  geom_bar(position='dodge',col='black')+
  labs(
    title="Distribution of Payment Mode within Fraudulent/Legal Transactions",
    y = "Count",
    x= "0=Legal 1=Fraud"
  )+
  scale_y_continuous()+
  theme_minimal()
```

This is a barchart of the amount of fraudulent/nonfradulent transactions filled by payment type (1=Fraudulent). It seems that the payment type is evenly distributed in both fraudulent and legal transactions.
